questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(4,-1,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(4,-1,3):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2})k \\  & =x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j-2z\text{ }k \\ ∇f(4,-1,3) & =(4)\text{ }i+2(-1)\text{ }j-2(3)\text{ }k \\  & =4i-2j-6k \\  & =⟨4,\,-2,\,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(4,-1,3)\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-(-1),\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-2,\,-6⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y+1,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-4)-2(y+1)-6(z-3) & =0 \\ 4x-2y-6z & =0 \\ 2x-y-3z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}$,  find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,1,1):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}+2{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =2x\text{ }i+8y\text{ }j+4z\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(2,1,1) & =2(2)\text{ }i+8(1)j+4(1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i+8\,j+4\,k \\  & =⟨4,8,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇\,f(2,1,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,8,4⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-2)+8(y-1)+4(z-1) & =0 \\ 4x+8y+4z-20 & =0 \\ x+2y+z-5 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{3}{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,-1,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{3}{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }i+(2y{x}^{3}+{z}^{2})\text{ }j+2yzk \\ ∇\,f(1,-1,1) & =3(1)^{2}(-1)^{2}\text{ }i+(\,2(-1)(1)^{3}+(1)^{2}\,)\text{ }j+2(-1)(1)k \\  & =3\,i-1\,j-2k \\  & =⟨3,-1,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-1,1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨3,-1,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+1,\,z-1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz$,  find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-1,-1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,-1,-1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}-xz)\text{ }k \\  & =(2xy-z)\text{ }i+({x}^{2}+2y)\text{ }j-xk \\ ∇\,f(2,-1,-1) & =(\,2(2)(-1)-(-1)\,)\text{ }i+(\,{2}^{2}+2(-1)\,)\text{ }j-2k \\  & =-3\,i+2\,j-2\,k \\  & =⟨-3,2,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,-1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-3,2,-2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+1,\,z+1⟩ & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=xy-yz-xz$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes  through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,3,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(2,3,4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy-yz-xz)\text{ }k \\  & =(y-z)\text{ }i+(x-z)\text{ }j+(-y-x)k \\ ∇\,f(2,3,4) & =(3-4)\text{ }i+(2-4)\text{ }j+(-3-2)k \\  & =-1\text{ }i-2\text{ }j-5k \\  & =⟨-1,-2,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(2,3,4)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨-1,-2,-5⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-3,\,z-4⟩ & =0 \\ -(x-2)-2(y-3)-5(z-4) & =0 \\ -x-2y-5z+28 & =0 \\ x+2y+5z-28 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Tangent Plane of a Surface Given Implicitly Using the Gradient Vector
questions.problem: Consider the surface $\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{3}+yz)=3.$ Given that $n=⟨a,b,c⟩$ is a non-zero normal vector to the surface at the point $(e,{e}^{2},-e),$ what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's define  $f(x,y,z)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{3}+yz).$ Then, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=3.$  

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(e,{e}^{2},-e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{3}+yz))i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{3}+yz))j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(2{x}^{3}+yz))k \\  & =(\frac{1}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\cdot 6{x}^{2})i+(\frac{1}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\cdot z)j+(\frac{1}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\cdot y)k \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\text{ }i+\frac{z}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\text{ }j+\frac{y}{2{x}^{3}+yz}\text{ }k \\ ∇f(e,{e}^{2},-e) & =\frac{6{e}^{2}}{2{e}^{3}+{e}^{2}(-e)}\text{ }i+\frac{(-e)}{2{e}^{3}+{e}^{2}(-e)}\text{ }j+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2{e}^{3}+{e}^{2}(-e)}\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{6}{e}\text{ }i-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}\text{ }j+\frac{1}{e}\text{ }k \\  & =⟨\frac{6}{e},\,-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}},\,\frac{1}{e}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our normal vector is $n=⟨a,b,c⟩=⟨\frac{6}{e},\,-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}},\,\frac{1}{e}⟩.$

Finally, $\frac{a}{b}=\frac{(\frac{6}{e})}{(-\frac{1}{{e}^{2}})}=-6e.$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $z{x}^{3}=-1+x{y}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,-2,3).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z{x}^{3} & =-1+x{y}^{2} \\ z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-1.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,-2,3):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{x}^{3}-x{y}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(3{x}^{2}z-{y}^{2})\text{ }i-2xy\text{ }j+{x}^{3}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,-2,3) & =(3(1)^{2}(3)-(-2)^{2})\text{ }i-2(1)(-2)\text{ }j+(1)^{3}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i+4\,j+1\,k \\  & =⟨5,4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,-2,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-(-2),\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,4,1⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y+2,\,z-3⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x-1)+4(y+2)+(z-3) & =0 \\ 5x+4y+z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface ${x}^{2}=-xyz.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(4,2,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & =-xyz \\ {x}^{2}+xyz & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+xyz$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

 

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(4,2,-2):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+xyz)\text{ }k \\  & =(2x+yz)\text{ }i+xz\text{ }j+xy\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(4,2,-2) & =(2(4)+2(-2))\text{ }i+4(-2)\text{ }j+4(2)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i-8j+8\,k \\  & =⟨4,-8,8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(4,2,-2)\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-2,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,-8,8⟩\cdot ⟨x-4,\,y-2,\,z+2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-4)+(-8)(y-2)+8(z+2) & =0 \\ 4x-8y+8z+16 & =0 \\ x-2y+2z+4=0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $z{e}^{x}+xy={x}^{2}.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(-1,1,2e).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}z{e}^{x}+xy & ={x}^{2} \\ z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2}$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=0.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,1,2e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(z{e}^{x}+xy-{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(z{e}^{x}+y-2x)\text{ }i+x\text{ }j+{e}^{x}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,1,2e) & =((2e){e}^{-1}+1-2(-1))\text{ }i+(-1)\text{ }j+{e}^{-1}\text{ }k \\  & =5\,i-j+{e}^{-1}\,k \\  & =⟨5,-1,{e}^{-1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,1,2e)\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1,\,z-2e⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨5,-1,{e}^{-1}⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-1,\,z-2e⟩ & =0 \\ 5(x+1)+(-1)(y-1)+{e}^{-1}(z-2e) & =0 \\ 5x-y+{e}^{-1}z+4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Consider the surface $xy{z}^{2}=6-z.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to that surface at the point $(1,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}xy{z}^{2} & =6-z \\ xy{z}^{2}+z & =6\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z)=xy{z}^{2}+z$, our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=6.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(1,1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xy{z}^{2}+z)\text{ }k \\  & =(y{z}^{2})\text{ }i+(x{z}^{2})\text{ }j+(2xyz+1)\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,2) & =(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }i+(1)(2)^{2}\text{ }j+(2(1)(1)(2)+1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i+4j+5\,k \\  & =⟨4,4,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,2)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,4,5⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z-2⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-1)+4(y-1)+5(z-2) & =0 \\ 4x+4y+5z-18 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z) = x^2+y^2+z^2,$ find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(2,-2,1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla \! f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(x_0,y_0,z_0) =(2,-2,1)\mathbin{:}$  

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}\,i+{f}_{y}\,j+{f}_{z}\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =2x\text{ }i+2y\text{ }j+2z\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(2,-2,1) & =2(2)\text{ }i+2(-2)\text{ }j+2(1)\text{ }k \\  & =4\,i-4\,j+2\text{ }k \\  & =⟨4,\,-4\,,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇\,f(2,-2,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y-(-2),\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨4,\,-4,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,\,y+2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 4(x-2)-4(y+2)+2(z-1) & =0 \\ 4x-4y+2z-18 & =0 \\ 2x-2y+z-9 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Tangent Plane of a Surface Given Implicitly Using the Gradient Vector
canonical_examples.problem: Consider the surface $z^3y^2 =x^2-5.$ Find the equation of the tangent plane to this surface at the point $(-1,2,-1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{3}{y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-5 \\ {z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y,z) = z^3y^2 - x^2,$ our surface can be viewed as the level surface $f(x,y,z)=-5.$ 

Recall that the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z) = k$ at the point $(x_0,y_0,z_0)$ can be expressed as

$$
\nabla f(x_0,y_0,z_0) \cdot \langle x-x_0, \: y-y_0, \: z-z_0 \rangle  = 0.
$$

Now, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $(-1,2,-1)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({z}^{3}{y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\text{ }k \\  & =(-2x)\text{ }i+2{z}^{3}y\text{ }j+3{z}^{2}{y}^{2}\text{ }k \\ ∇\,f(-1,2,-1) & =(-2)(-1)\text{ }i+2(-1)^{3}(2)\text{ }j+3(-1)^{2}(2)^{2}\text{ }k \\  & =2\,i-4j+12\,k \\  & =⟨2,-4,12⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(-1,2,-1)\cdot ⟨x-(-1),\,y-2,\,z-(-1)⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2,-4,12⟩\cdot ⟨x+1,\,y-2,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2(x+1)-4(y-2)+12(z+1) & =0 \\ 2x-4y+12z+22 & =0 \\ x-2y+6z+11 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
